channel.title: Boulder Daily Camera - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Boulder Daily Camera (dailycamera.com)

item.title: Lawyers of Chicago woman shot by federal agents say documents show how DHS lies about investigations
item.description: Marimar Martinez was shot five times by a Border Patrol agent in October while in her vehicle.

item.title: U.S. Rep. Jason Crow says ‘there will be costs’ to Trump officials after failed indictment attempt
item.description: "We are taking names, we are making lists," U.S. Rep. Jason Crow of Colorado said in an interview Wednesday, a day after federal prosecutors failed to win an indictment against him and other lawmakers.

item.title: Colorado sues to block Trump administration from cutting public health grants
item.description: The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services notified Congress it wouldn't pay $600 million worth of grants already awarded in Colorado, California, Illinois and Minnesota.

item.title: Longmont City Council approves fireworks funding for Fourth of July
item.description: Council members debate ticketed July 3 concert and vote 5–2 to allocate up to $45,000 for fireworks alongside drone show

item.title: Member of Trump’s Religious Liberty Commission ousted in dispute over antisemitism
item.description: The ousted member, Carrie Prejean Boller, had defended commentator Candace Owens.

item.title: ‘A Century of Jazz in Colorado’ comes to Longmont Museum
item.description: Five Points Ambassadors to honor 100 years of jazz and the legacies of Charles Burrell and Purnell Steen in Feb. 12 concert.

item.title: CU Buffs women’s basketball holds off Houston for Big 12 road win
item.description: HOUSTON – Colorado had to sweat more than it wanted in the closing minutes, but got the result it wanted.

item.title: No. 16 Texas Tech crushes reeling CU Buffs
item.description: There was no stirring comeback this time. And the end result was the same as it has been in each of Colorado’s most recent road outings.

item.title: Rockies’ starting rotation competition bolstered by three veteran free agents
item.description: Bolstered by the acquisition of three veteran free agents -- right-hander Michael Lorenzen and Tomoyuki Sugano, and lefty Jose Quintana -- the Rockies open spring training on Thursday at Salt River Fields in Scottsdale, Ariz., with plenty of competition for the starting rotation.

item.title: Colorado duo Bangot Dak, Sebastian Rancik continue to struggle on road
item.description: For the first time in four games, forwards Bangot Dak and Sebastian Rancik both were in the starting lineup.
